look_here_first: Inspect opposite paired leaves along a creeping, node-rooting stem. Look for very small yellow petals (when present), but note they may be shed or naturally absent. Crucially, a mature capsule lacks the four dark-green longitudinal bands seen on L. palustris. Do not force submerged sterile specimens to species.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: opposite paired leaves on creeping wetland stems, shared with palustris

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: tiny usually yellow four-petaled axillary flower, but petals may be absent

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mature 4-angled capsule LACKS the four longitudinal dark-green bands of palustris

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: same vegetative architecture as palustris; use mature fruit confirmation when petals absent

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Aquatic perennial, creeping to ascending, sometimes submerged, forming loose mats with adventitious roots at nodes.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Shiny elliptic to obovate or lance-elliptic leaves, often short-petioled but with variable petiole length; blades commonly 0.8–4.5 cm long (FNA).

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Tiny axillary flowers usually with four small pale-yellow/yellow petals and four stamens. Petals are caducous and sometimes absent; the absence of petals alone does NOT establish L. palustris.

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey's San Marcos River sequence shows the submerged/creeping form in situ, a useful contrast with the erect shoreline habit of Ludwigia octovalvis.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Mostly cylindric, often reddish, little or no hair; may root where creeping stem touches moist sediment.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Opposite, usually decussate pairs at each node; primary distinction from alternate-leaved Ludwigia octovalvis.

key_traits.label: Ovary
key_traits.text: Short inferior green ovary, about 1.5 mm in local specimens, strongly four-angled and roughly funnel-shaped; beneath tiny sepals, often hard to see without macro.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Mature capsule often 4–10 mm long (FNA; local Williamson account may be narrower), 4-angled, without longitudinal green bands on the four faces. Contrast L. palustris shorter often 2–5 mm green-banded capsule; sizes overlap.
